item.title: [Seeking Greenlights] What Follows
item.description: So yknow that thing that makes you need to run up the stairs in the dark?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:
"What Follows" is, to put it in the most basic terms possible, what makes you need to run up the stairs whenever it is dark. The SCP itself is theorized to reside in the human psychospace, which is why it is such a widespread phenomenon among humans. While the SCP itself is the feeling of fear when walking up a dark staircase, the actual danger of it comes from it's secondary instance, which attacks whichever unfortunate person has chosen to not run up the stairs in time (Not always resulting in death).

Central Narrative:
Containment procedures begin the article with the possibility of the SCP residing in the human psychospace, as well as the fact that the primary instance of the SCP cannot be contained, with the Foundation's main way of containment being a public misinformation campaign. Throughout the article, it is increasingly alluded to that the SCP is more than a simple fight-or-flight response to a monster under the stairs, but could be a breakthrough in unlocking greater human potential, ad even the ability to see into the near future.

Collaps'd (More below)
Uncollaps'd

Most of the following would be shown through addendums and interview logs:
With the possibility of such important breakthroughs, upper foundation staff decide to begin a special research project on the matter. The actual project name is redacted, giving the reader the possibility that it may actually be project PNEUMA (and therefor might lead to the O-5's decision to terminate humanity). The actual end result of the project isn't revealed, with it only being alluded to that it didn't go well, so that the reader is left with a sense of mystery as to exactly what the foundation learned.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Just to start off, the article opens with a note from the Containment Committee on reallocating more staff towards the research of this entity, as well as the Containment Procedure itself stating that the primary instance of the SCP cannot be contained.

Additional Notes:
I've never been good at voicing my thoughts, so just to make it clear: The SCP is the feeling of fear itself when walking up a dark staircase, with it's secondary instance being the actual attack from behind.

item.title: House of Memories
item.description: When there's a magical family secret to be uncovered, sometimes you have to go on a trip down memory lane.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Just your typical SCP article layout. Some interviews, some exploration logs, maybe a few notes, I dunno. That's something for me to handle during the drafting phase.

As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices...
...please collapse long posts.

Elevator Pitch: A house that causes you to experience past memories (or just past experiences in your life, doesn't really matter if you remember it). It'll normally attempt to lure you in by using creatures that trick you into believing that people you trust are asking you to go inside, primarily by shapeshifting. The main creature1 luring you in is trapped inside the house and can create other creatures2 to go outside and lure you in for it if necessary. It will keep trying until it gets tired or finds more suitable prey. Once you're in, you become one of the minions of the main creature inhabiting the house.

Central Narrative: So… some kids messed up. Basically, a kid's grandmother told him about a spell that could curse households. Reason? Not important. What's important is that you can't trust kids with magic. That kid went and told all his friends about it, and they thought it would be funny if they cursed this one house on a mountain.

Oh yeah, did I mention kids are really bad at using magic? In fact, they're so bad that one of the kids in the friend group got cursed along with the house and was forced to inhabit it forever3. After the spell was cast, the Foundation detected anomalous activity on a mountain… somewhere. Haven't decided yet. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

Anyway, the Foundation took the kids in and gave them amnestics, but… it didn't work. Because of how the curse functions, it wouldn't allow them to forget about it. The Foundation had no choice but to take care of them until they were old enough to become Class-D Personnel.

All of those events set up the Foundation's investigations on why the house was what it was. The Class-D were used for explorations and it revealed more about the grandmother (yeah, remember her?) and her relations to their family's history with magic and anomalies.

Hook/Attention Grabber: I guess it could be the small mistake of some negligent kids unraveling a family's anomalous secrets. The chain reaction could be somewhat interesting.

Additional Notes: While ambitious for a first-time SCP writer, the magical history of the family could be a nice setup for a GoI. I wouldn't get too excited about that yet though. :)

Also, I would like some attention on my hook, as I'm kind of struggling with it.

Footnotes
1. SCP-XXXX-1
2. SCP-XXXX-2 instances
3. This is SCP-XXXX-1

item.title: SCP-The Mimic
item.description: An idea for an SCP me and my brother came up with.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: The SCP is a humanoid entity similar to SCP-096, being tall, disproportionate, and skinny. The SCP can produce any sound at any volume at any location, as long as it's heard it before. There are also two other parts of the SCP. The village it came from is the first, it's an endless maze of houses and shops, some buildings being made of obscure materials, including glass, wires, and human components. The other part of the SCP are people who have seen the entity through photography or video. The go crazy a few hours after seeing the image or video, and kill any living thing they see, but can't die themselves.

Central Narrative: After reports came that an entire village had been wiped out, the foundation investigated, and found the entity in the forest near by, and brought it into containment. They also discovered the anomalous effects of the village. Then, after taking pictures of the SCP, and showing them to a few people, those people went crazy, and those anomalous effects were discovered.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The physical description, and the ability of the entity grabs attention, as it's very obscure and slightly scary. The description and ability of the village and the crazy people also add to it, as they are also pretty freaky, and generally disturbing. It may not be extremely significant, but it adds as a whole to the scp world.

item.title: SCP-XXXX Where the Heart is
item.description: Shared pain and experiences can bring people closer together
item.content:encoded:
Shared pain and experiences can bring people closer together, who doesn't want that!? Something else wants to attain its former glory - there seem to be some "win-win" situations here.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre: Horror?

Elevator Pitch:

  • A creature that haunts Christmas as well as Halloween
  • Object Class: Keter For its innumerable ways of evading capture, enclosures, and personnel
  • There are three types of encounters (with the main entity specifically), they are:
    • Black Events: Where the ritualistic consumption of a child is done by the child's family, along with the entity during Halloween
    • White Events: Causes a family to become closer to each other as serial murders after SCP-XXXX is taken in (while posing as a homeless person)
    • Red Events: Are when it's outside of a Black or White Event and gouges out the heart of a person(s)
+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The creature was once one of the "Faces of the Holidays", namely Halloween. With a competitive and impulsive nature, it ate the heart of "Christmas" - becoming a being that encompasses both holidays. Though this caused it to become even more unstable, now consuming the hearts of 'innocents' to regain its purity in its madness.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: While the creature seems very violent, it sometimes leaves people better than before: having a better outlook on life and being an overall better person.

Don't let that small chance of salvation fool you though - while its intentions may not be evil, what it does is extremely traumatizing.

Additional Notes: I did NOT include all of the context/info with these events and capabilities to make it easily digestible in this format.

This is my first time making one of these… so yeah, thanks for reading and tell me if there's anything I did wrong here; or if there are any questions :)


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts and properly space your paragraphs. ~Zyn

item.title: SCP Greenlight Idea
item.description: An anomalous metal dog crate that actively hunts family pets
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre (Optional): Horror-ish

Elevator Pitch: An anomalous, predatory dog crate.

Central Narrative: A dog crate, which lures in pets and then eats them. By all normal appearances, it is a normal dog crate. But when left alone in a room with an animal, (non-human) it will manifest inside it a toy or some object that the animal will be attracted to. If the animal enters the cage, the door will shut behind it and the crate will eat the pet. Despite being made of metal, the crate still feels pain and reacts to external stimuli. (Largely by slamming the door open and shut, but it can make noises) If placed in a not ideal location for finding prey, the crate can relocate itself by rolling on its side to a new place. The make, model, and ID Number on it correlate to a crate sold by a company, and records show it was sold to a circus infamous for animal cruelty (Revised) (I'm admittedly considering scrapping the idea, but if anyone thinks it has potential, I'll see what I can do.)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A non-biological predator that preys on pain, hunts and kills sweet family pets, and has developed a merciless camouflage system.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: 432.7 Hz
item.description: An anomalous tone that seems to not be sound, and yet people perceive it as such
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This "sound" spreads across a roughly 2km radius, only detectable by people, regardless of hearing ability. The sound is mobile, and the only seeming means of containment is to create louder sounds around it to cover its presence.

Central Narrative: The foundation invests heavy amount of resources into containment, as the "sound" is mobile, moving at a slow pace of about 3km/hr. The foundation has surmised that organizing parades or construction work is the best means in order to contain it in high populous zones. The conflict arises when some individuals try to create art surrounding the "sound", playing instruments or singing in harmony with it. Although no ill-effects are seen from this, the foundation still attempts to stop any such performances in order to maintain containment.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Strange mobile sound that the foundation struggles to contain, while others who notice it try and embrace it. Calls into question the legitimacy of the lengths the foundation will go to contain relatively benign anomalies.

Additional Notes: Deciding the class I feel might be a bit hard, as I feel like it may be Keter due to its generally hard to contain nature, however it could be Euclid I suppose too

item.title: SCP Idea: The Plastic Army
item.description: Heavily revised version of one of my old ideas
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Drama/Emotional, History

Page Layout: The page will have the basic SCP article layout, but with addendums sharing the development of the army’s story.

Elevator Pitch: A collection of living Gundam models. Have organs underneath the plastic armor plates, but they do not match any living species. The models speak in the memories of American soldiers in the Vietnam War that seem to be from another timeline.

Central Narrative: Tells the story of American soldiers in the Vietnam War. The models were found in a former Vietnamese battlefield with significant damage. On the surface, there is nothing particularly strange about them. However, there appear to be functioning organs beneath the plastic armor plates that do not match up to any known species. Although they appear to be human-like, they contain DNA that varies greatly from those of humans. The living parts of all of the models are of the same species. The models cannot move, but they are known to speak. It speaks from the perspective of several soldiers such as General Richard Hall from the dates of November 8, 1955, to May 9, 1961. It begins with Richard Hall getting drafted, and later the other soldiers are seen getting drafted. The story from here on out consists mostly dialogue between the models, shouting during battles, and various promotions. At any points in time where a bodily fluid would be excreted by one of the soldiers, the model excretes the same fluid. Recorded excretions include blood, sweat, tears, and urine. Although the story encompasses almost seven years, the full seven years are not played out. Only select days are played out. These days include battles, significant interactions, and promotions. The full day is always played out. On the final day, there is a battle that all of the soldiers take part in. In this battle, they each comment on a creature that looks somewhat like a dog before dying. Upon death, they bleed profusely for 5 minutes before the organs cease function. After 214 hours, the story begins again the exact same way, in a cyclical nature. The real versions of these soldiers all had different positions. They all died on July 24, 2006.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Emotional story told by Gundams.

Additional Notes: I just really want this to be its best, since I'm not a super experienced writer.

item.title: SCP-XXXX "The Nightmare Victim"
item.description: appears in the nightmares of her victims
item.content:encoded:
A bloodied, nude woman (don't worry, the blood covers anything inappropriate) that appears in the nightmares of her victims.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch:

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX appears to be a bloody, nude female entity (blood covers any extremities) with multiple stab wounds that appears in the nightmares of distinct individuals. Nearly all subjects reported seeing copious amounts of blood pouring out of said wounds.

All relevant data has been collected by interviewing test subjects (D-Class) directly exposed to SCP-XXXX-1, a handcrafted knife from the 14th century, after multiple sleep studies.

Central Narrative

+ show block
– hide block

90% of encounters follow this path; The subject walks into a dark room with bloody tools and knives lining the walls. In the center of the room is a table on which SCP-XXXX lies. Upon approaching the table, 100% of subjects reported that the figure began to rise from of the table and approach them.

SCP-XXXX-1 seems to have a strong connection to SCP-XXXX, possibly the weapon that killed it in the first place. The weapon had traces of blood in which the DNA of a young woman named "Vivian Fay" was extracted.

Hook/Attention Grabber:

+ show block
– hide block

Contact with SCP-XXXX has been reported to cause several health issues, such as heart palpitations, unprovoked panic attacks and restricted airways, even in young, healthy individuals with no pre-existing conditions. In extreme cases it causes cerebral hemorrhaging and unexplainable chest wounds.

item.title: Moonbug
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Sci-fi

Page Layout (Optional): Standard layout. Containment procedure, Description, addendums

Elevator Pitch: Object makes impact with moon and researchers at Lunar Area-32 find a parasitic lifeform with anomalous properties in the substance left by the object.

Central Narrative: A object collides with the moon not far from Lunar Area-32 and a team sets out to investigate it. At the impact site they find a crater with a dark substance from which they take samples and return to base. Further study of the substance shows that it contains a parasite that will enter the human body through a body opening or wound and attach to the brain stem. Once attached the host will experience anomalous effects.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's a quite simple story that I hope to make interesting through exploration of the SCP and it's effects, and possibly how it could be used to the foundations benefit,

Additional Notes:

item.title: Good intentions
item.description: A semi-sentient liquid metal that tries to protect his host
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A semi-sentient liquid metal that bonds with a persons nervous system and tries to protect that person from harm, but ultimately does more harm than good.

Central Narrative: The SCP is an unknown liquid metal that enters a persons body through the skin, bonding with that persons nervous system. Whenever an object/person comes into contact with the skin of the host, the metal will rush through the persons nerves to the point of impact, surfacing out of the skin to form a shield that protects the person from physical trauma. The SCP accidentally damages the nerves when it travels through them, causing intense pain in the host in the short run, and loss of fine motor skills to loss of all feelings in limbs in the long run. Even if the SCP is inactive in the host, over time the host will develop symptoms similar to long-term mercury poisoning, which will result in death after 10-15 months.

+ show
- hide

The SCP will only have one host at a time, and will not transfer to another while the previous host still lives. It initially transfers by skin to skin contact with the previous hosts corpse, however if the SCP is without a host for an extended period of time, it will leave the previous hosts body and seek out the nearest human to bond with. If it is unable to find a host after leaving the previous host, it will become increasingly aggressive and stronger to break out and locate a new host.

Due to the SCP reacting to even the smallest contacts with the skin, it becomes nigh impossible for the host to complete small tasks, and even a small shift in their clothing can set of the SCP. Monitoring the effects the SCP has on its hosts is extremely difficult, because the SCP prevents the foundation from taking any samples while the host still lives, and most forms of scans are ineffective.

In order to contain the anomaly, the foundation will expose a D-class in a medically induced coma to the SCP, and try to keep them alive for as long as possible. After the death of the D-class, a new D-class will be put into a coma before transferring the SCP to them.


Hook/Attention-Grabber: Something created to protect humans ends up damaging them in the long run.

Additional Notes: Linked to the broken god.

item.title: SCP Idea: The Earworm
item.description: What if that song stuck in your head, was more than just a song stuck in your head?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes
Page Type: SCP article
Genre: Horror
Page Layout: Basic, Containment Procedures, Description of SCPs effects, than 2 interview logs and an incident report detailing a mass outbreak of the SCP.
Elevator Pitch: An human infecting parasite that is activated by song.

The Earworm is a keter class entity due to it being a small difficult to spot, wide spread parasitic entity capable of emitting a cognitohazardous noise.

Earworms will hang in bushes and form cacoons in the shape of small music notes, at which point they will begin produce a song.

The Earworm's song compels those who hear it to eat it, at which point, the stomach acids will dissolve the cacoon and Earworm will burrow out of the stomach and make it's way to the brain, burrowing into the left side of the cerebrum then inject an amnestic so the host forgets eating the cacoon. It will remain there in a hibernating state until the host hears music.

+ show block
– hide block

Once the host hears music, the Earworm will awaken and begin eating the hosts Cerebellum, growing in size and connecting to the Host's nervous system. During this process the host will be unable to get the song that activated the earworm out of their head.

Over time, the Earworm will eat and replace more and more of the hosts brain, eventually removing the ability for complex thought and turning the host into a feral creature incapable of speaking in anything other than the song. At this point the Earworm, now resembling brain tissue itself, will lay eggs in the remains of the hosts brain and the host will be drawn to populated yet rural areas. Once the eggs hatch the Earworm larvae will eat the rest of the hosts brain and burrow out to find a place where they can make a cacoon.

This leaves the host completely under control of the now adult Earworm, which has completely replaced the hosts brain.

Hook: The idea is to start of with a relatable experience (A song being so stuck in your head) and make you question yourself every time you experience it.

item.title: The Metempsychosis Monstrosity
item.description: A sentient eldritch mound of flesh that has the soul of its last victim pilot its body
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A giant formless fleshy monstrosity living in the a part of the Bering Sea. While immobile, the creature is sentient, and appears to be in a constant state of distress. When a living human victim is fed to the creature, it will expel the remains of its last victim, and its new victim will take over its body until a new one is fed to it.

Central Narrative: After discovering the creature and its property, the Foundation appoints General Ferguson in charge of containment, who quickly begins cracking down on the anomaly. Soon after, it is found that the SCP can communicate in simple sentences via a special radio frequency, and the foundation discovers that the anomaly is "hungry" and "hurting", and wants more victims so it can be freed. After this, Ferguson cracks down even more, building a massive concrete wall around the anomaly and ordering constant security, with no one to be anywhere near the creature or have any communication. While many researchers do attempt communication otherwise, they are unable to do much else to help it due to Ferguson's strict orders. Eventually, a d class ends up being fed to it, and there is a massive call among the other d class at the station to feed it another victim to save their comrade.

Hook/Attention Grabber: After this, Ferguson becomes even more strict, with anyone who sympathizes with the anomaly ordered to be imprisoned for treason against the Foundation. Eventually, years later, the anomaly finally moves from its position and makes a charge for Ferguson in a devastating containment breach, with Ferguson being consumed by the end. After this, nearby Foundation ships pick up distress signals from a scared and pained Ferguson calling for backup. The ships attempt to help, but after being met by heavy d class resistance at the station, they compromise with them and agree that the foundation is allowed back in the site as long as they don't help Ferguson, deciding that his tyrannical actions got him what he deserved.

Additional Notes: Hope this isn't too similar to anything else!

item.title: First SCP
item.description: Why has no one yet thought of an SCP with this property?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP

Genre (Optional):

Page Layout (Optional):

Elevator Pitch: The SCP is an extradimensional space that traps people inside if they know that the SCP exists. It was made as a containment vessel for something really dangerous.

Central Narrative: The SCP was created by an anomalous person to deal with a dangerous anomaly of yet unknown nature. Its properties ensure that knowledge of the SCP will never exist outside of it, therefore ensuring that the entity contained within will never be known to the outside world. The Foundation decides to investigate a series of disappearances which leads them to discover the SCP. When the MTF get inside they learn of the scip's effects from the person which results in them unable to leave the SCP. They compile a document describing the SCP before taking amnestics. The Amnestics removed their knowledge of the SCP, allowing them to return to site. When the SCP documentation is read, the reader will be immediately teleported to the SCP, requiring them to consume amnestics to leave.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I've not yet seen an SCP with effects which are caused by someone knowing them. It's just a very goood concept to think about. In fact, I don't know why I haven't read an SCP with this property, because it is just so obvious.

Additional Notes: The dangerous entity could be another SCP. This is just about the location that it is contained within and its property.
Also, I don't know how is the article going to work in-universe because everyone who reads the article and therefore becomes aware of the existence of the SCP will be pulled into it.

item.title: Requesting greenlight for SCP (Tune in Next Time)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mainly historical, a bit of horror, I suppose

Page Layout (Optional): Basic layout; containment procedures, test logs, possibly a picture

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a radio tower built somewhere around the 1980s located around Ballard, Utah, and has not been fed power since its abandonment somewhere between 1985 and 1990. The tower broadcasts a radio signal which is still able to be picked up by radios approximately six miles in the surrounding area. The signal is static at most times save for an AI voice announcing a web address every five hours. The address seems to be the contact information for the radio tower operators. But there have been four (4) recorded instances of there being an actual being speaking through the signal.

Central Narrative: When the static clears on the signal a being deemed SCP-XXXX-A speaks through the signal in a deep, muffled voice. In all cases of this occurring, the being has announced the first and last name of a person, followed by a word and a series of four seemingly random numbers after which the signal returns to static.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Within the time ranging from two hours to three weeks, the person which the name belongs is attacked by an anomalous creature. The hostility and overall danger of the creature vary with each encounter with some merely beating or bruising the victim, to consuming them. The time in which SCP-XXXX-A has existed is currently unknown with the first record of the being dating back to the early sixteen hundreds with an Englishman describing "a cloaked figure who sat at tavern tables requesting bizarre items in exchange for the punishment of another". SCP-XXXX-A is capable of being contacted currently through an email which is posted on SCP-XXXX's website. Three of the four people responsible for the recorded attacks have been subdued and administered class-B amnestics. The whereabouts of the last person are currently unknown.

Additional Notes: No additional notes.

item.title: The Silver Sludge
item.content:encoded:
Looking for green light: yep

Page type: SCP article

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is the classic grey goo monster. It’s a tall albino male that whenever they feel threatened or someone else is in the room with them will start secreting a silver sludge that will try to grapple onto the persons skin. After attaching my it will sink into the persons pores and start replacing all organic matter underneath the skin with the silver sludge. Within a minute the body will begin having seizures from the body rejecting the sludge. After a few minutes the seizures will end and the person will be entirely controlled by the SCP. The SCP is sapient and has full control over the sludge no matter how far away it is

item.title: The Oreads
item.description: After a Battle So Great, all that remains is Dust.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): History, Fantasy

Page Layout (Optional): ACS

+ Idea here
- Long, I know

Elevator Pitch: SCP is a small, 50m long beach located near Kandestederne, Denmark. In the event an individual makes contact with the sand, it will respond to the conscious thoughts of that individual and shift into a variety of structures accordingly. With concentration, The sand can also emulate the structures physical (not chemical) properties, such as weight, ductility, pigment and conductivity. However, it can't take the form of non-solids. The sand only acts this way if it's on the beach. If the sand is taken 5 meters away from the beach, the sand will start vibrating and pulsating before suddenly becoming inactive. The sand also appears to have some degree of sapience/conscious and can react if communicated with or attacked.

Central Narrative: When the Foundation first discovered the beach (in the 1950s), it was acting aggressive and attacked anyone who attempted to walk upon it. Through research and discussions with the locals, the Foundation discover one of them is in possession of a jar of sand which they took from the beach after discovering it's strange properties. The sand was then returned and the beach instantly began cooperating.

After some experiments with the sand, researchers managed to discover it could understand Koine Greek. After finding a translater, the Foundation were able to discover that the sand is in fact the remnants of the Oread, the mountain nymphs from Greek Mythology. The Oreads reveal that long ago, they lost their true form in a battle with a monstrous sea creature1, resulting in them taking on their current sand from. In their sand form, they're conscious was spread so thin, only they're instinct to join back together remained. This was difficult as their parts were spread across the world via ocean currents. The beach is a collection of their remnants who've managed to form a collective conscious. However, it's weak enough to be influenced by a stronger mind, resulting in the structures it creates.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This article is kind of sad. We're meant to feel sorry for the Oreads. They desperately want to return to their old forms but The Foundation is unable to help as 1. it would take forever for every sand particle to randomly end up on the beach and 2. how can The Foundation possibly give them back their true form if they don't know who's who and what they look like.

item.title: Hackerman B)
item.description: Its me, the anonymous masked guy!
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Starts with a hacking section (just scroll through with colors really), reveal information as it goes, and at the end have a post escape file.

Elevator Pitch: Anomaly is pretty boring, a guy with pure black skin, no facial features, and when someone tries to reveal, learn, etc, information about them, they spoil the plot of something for them by sending them a mental image, video, or other. Also a better hacker than the foundations best. The narrative is where the meat of this is.

Central Narrative: The article starts in first person, with you as the SCP, and has you follow them along an escape attempt. This will be full of bread crumbs about the SCP in question to keep the reader invested, as well as all sorts of shenanigans. Their thoughts will be shown to add more immersion. After it all ends, you finally get the full story with a post escape SCP File.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It quickly gets into the escape section, which is where the action is.

Additional Notes: Associated with gamers against weed, which will also let me slip some more comedic elements in.

item.title: [Seeking Greenlight] A sentient entity formed from a psychic virus
item.description: experiences the sensations of every infected person
item.content:encoded:
An otherwise benign virus, present in nearly every human, creates a sentient entity which experiences the sensations of every infected person.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Drama/ (maybe) Comedy

Page Layout: Since this would be my first SCP, it will remain simple, with standard containment/description and a couple addendums.

Elevator Pitch: Nearly every human hosts a benign virus, located in their brain, which emits psychic signals to virus cells in other hosts. These cells combine, like neurons in a brain, to form a sentient entity. This entity experiences the sensory inputs of every infected individual, motivating it to act in the interest of maximizing human pleasure and minimizing human pain. The entity is able to "possess" the bodies of a small number of infected humans at a time, and uses this ability to communicate.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: Containment procedures will first outline Foundation contingency plans for vaccinating all staff and the general population, before detailing the process of the Foundation conducting yearly negotiations with the the entity for its cooperation. The result of these negotiations is an agreement wherein the entity assists the foundation through its abilities, while the Foundation takes limited actions to influence national and international politics in ways the entity believes will increase collective happiness. The entity has over the years made increasingly extreme demands, and the Foundation privately fears they create a high risk of exposure. Addendums include conversations with the entity, as well as the text of the agreement between it and the Foundation

Hook/Attention-Grabber: As a result of experiencing vast sensory input from large numbers of people, the entity has a unique personality and manner of speaking, constantly switching languages and often communicating in references to popular culture (i.e. quotes from widely-viewed movies, news and sports broadcasts, and printed media). The entity also has a skewed view of humanity, discounting freedom of action in favor of collective interests.

Additional Notes:

1. Considering adding a comedic edge to the story by having the entity be obsessed with a revival of its favorite television show, "The Andy Griffith Show," demanding that the Foundation resurrect the show's dead cast members so that new episodes can be viewed by the infected public.

2. I don't think this concept is particularly original, and don't have exhaustive knowledge of the SCP database, so please tell me if this has already been done in some form.

3. I have already written the first draft of an article, so if sharing that would be helpful to deciding whether or not to greenlight, please let me know.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: The Emotional Support Pet - Seeking Greenlights
item.description: A benefical Keter anomaly- has anyone done an idea like this already?
item.content:encoded:
The Emotional Support Pet

Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: What is the basic core idea? Use a bullet point list if necessary.

An adorable kitten, puppy or bunny who appears to meet people suffering from trauma, depression, or various other emotional and mental health issues, and who gets them to pet it, which causes the individual in question to heal from the issue until they no longer have need of such healing. In certain cases, such as in the case of abuse or situations serving to only exasperate the issues which the individual needs help with, the animal companion will align a series of events to extract the individual from the situation before the ensuing treatment.

Actually feeds off of both mental and emotional trauma as well as the excess positive energy which is produced during the healing process and for a short while afterwards. Doesn’t need to cause what it feeds off of and change from symbiosis to parasitism due to the huge number of people already suffering from these problems.

Class: Keter

Central Narrative: Helps to explain why humanity isn’t universally traumatized other than the low number of anomalous in the world, because there’s a huge amount and this world needs some form of anomalous therapist, of which there are far too few already.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Unsure, really only looking to post this idea if there isn’t already a similar enough instance to this prospective SCP. Mostly a hurt/comfort idea, but it can easily veer into horror if the anomalous object sees that the only way to fully heal the individual includes such events.

Additional Notes: Due to its teleportation to its ‘patients’ and how it literally bends probability to its own ends, which just so happy to most often be beneficial to humanity, as well as the unknown number of instances of this ‘species’ in this world, how do you think this would even be contained? Would it? And, again, has someone already written something like this?

So, this is my first potential contribution, so what do you guys think?
